newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins drift down on U.S, rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins drift down on U.S, rate hike fears.

text.p: MinFin bonds, following Bradies, edged down on Tuesday in quiet trading on uncertainty over a possible U.S. interest rate hike next week, dealers said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on March 25 to deliberate interest rates.
"Prices are easing but the decline is slow, and the volume traded is not high," Avtobank dealer Alla Zakharova said.
She said that the fourth and sixth tranches were the most traded, tracked by the 2008 maturity.
Dealers said the market was in a wait-and-see mood, with economists divided over whether the U.S. Fed will raise short-term rates to try to ward off inflation.
"The situation is nervous and uncertain," Aljba Alliance Bank dealer Sergei Seryogin said. "The market has no direction at the moment and can go any way."
He said the current decline could also be due to position-closing ahead of the FOMC meeting, speculative selling or filling client orders.
